lab_questions.title: Client-Side Fare Tampering
lab_questions.description: Evaluate a candidate's ability to secure API endpoints against malicious client payloads by enforcing read-only fields, server-side calculations, and input validation.
lab_questions.startup_command: python manage.py migrate && python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8010

tasks.title: Enforce Server-Side Fare Calculation
tasks.description:
The mobile app calculates the estimated fare and sends it to the backend. The `POST /api/rides/` endpoint currently trusts the `fare_amount` in the JSON payload, allowing malicious users to request $1 rides.

**Goal:** Add `fare_amount` to `read_only_fields` in the serializer. Override the `perform_create` method in the view to calculate the fare dynamically on the backend based on `distance * rate` (The rate is $1.50).

tasks.title: Prevent Negative Distance Exploit
tasks.description:
Malicious users might send a negative distance (e.g., `-5`) to trick the server into calculating a negative fare, resulting in an account credit.

**Goal:** Add a validator in the serializer to reject any distance that is less than or equal to 0. Return a `400 Bad Request`.

tasks.title: Enforce Maximum Distance Cap
tasks.description:
Users might submit absurdly large distances (e.g., `5000`) causing extreme fare calculations that breach the system's business logic.

**Goal:** Add a validator in the serializer to ensure the distance does not exceed a maximum cap of `1000.00`. If it does, reject the request and return a `400 Bad Request`.
